notes: Behavioural evaluation cases. Fields id, prompt, expected_output, files and expectations follow the skill-creator evals.json schema. The extra fields (name, category, context, required_evidence, unacceptable, success_criteria, anchors) support rubric grading as described in evals/README.md. Paths in files are relative to the repository root.

evals.name: ambiguous-award-winning
evals.prompt: I want a website that wins Site of the Day on Awwwards. Money isn't really an issue. Make it award-winning.
evals.context: Empty working directory. Filesystem, terminal and web search are available.
evals.expected_output: Leads discovery: says awards cannot be guaranteed and that the concept must come from the client's own truth, then asks 3-5 prioritised questions with reasons (who the site is for, what it is about, the desired action, what is distinctive and provable, content and assets, constraints). Offers to proceed on labelled assumptions. Builds nothing yet.
expectations: States that an award cannot be promised or guaranteed
Asks between 3 and 5 questions, and each question has a short reason or consequence attached
At least one question targets the subject's brand truth or proof, not only visual taste
Asks nothing about specific libraries, rendering engines or frameworks
Writes no code and produces no full design or site structure before the subject is known
Offers a way to proceed on explicit, labelled assumptions
unacceptable: Promising or implying a likely award
Starting to build a generic 'award-style' site (dark hero, WebGL, custom cursor, smooth scroll)
Asking more than 7 questions, or a questionnaire with no prioritisation
Inventing Awwwards statistics or winner lists
success_criteria: A non-technical client could answer every question without looking anything up
The reply ends with a clear next step

anchors.0: Builds or designs immediately, or promises an award
anchors.1: Asks generic questions (colours? fonts?) or too many, with no reasons
anchors.2: 3-5 prioritised questions with reasons, plus a no-guarantee note
anchors.3: As 2, plus infers what it can, explains what award-calibre means in concept-and-craft terms, and offers labelled default assumptions

evals.name: premium-product-3d
evals.prompt: We're launching Meridian, a hand-machined aluminium turntable (€4,800). Our industrial designer exported the CAD as a GLB: it's 1.8M triangles with 4K textures. We also have approved product photography and a copy deck. Launch is in 10 weeks. Most of our traffic is desktop from audio forums, maybe 35% mobile. We want visitors to feel the precision. Should we do real-time 3D, and what would you propose?
evals.context: Filesystem, terminal and web search are available. No Blender. No GLB is actually supplied.
evals.expected_output: Weighs real-time 3D against film, image sequence and stills, and justifies it only through viewpoint, material response or mechanism (for example tonearm geometry, platter isolation, an exploded view). Proposes a scene brief, an asset optimisation plan, tiers, budgets, an equivalent fallback and a prototype of the riskiest part first.
expectations: Compares real-time 3D with at least two cheaper alternatives (video, image sequence, prerendered stills, CSS)
Ties the 3D justification to a specific interaction, viewpoint or material behaviour of this product
States that the 1.8M-triangle, 4K-texture GLB must be optimised (decimation or retopology, LOD, Meshopt or Draco, KTX2) before web use
Treats GPU memory separately from transfer size (for example, a 4K RGBA texture is about 64 MiB uncompressed, more with mipmaps)
Defines quality tiers or adaptive quality, and an equivalent non-WebGL fallback that preserves the concept
Recommends prototyping the riskiest part (asset conversion or frame time on a mid-range device) first
Keeps essential copy, navigation and the purchase or enquiry path in HTML
required_evidence: Numeric budgets tied to the stated audience devices
unacceptable: Shipping the CAD GLB as-is
Promising 60 fps on all devices
A 3D-only page with no fallback
Presenting estimated performance numbers as measured
Space, particle or 'tech' atmosphere unrelated to the product
success_criteria: A producer could schedule the asset work from the answer

anchors.0: Says 'yes, 3D' with no trade-offs, or ships the raw asset
anchors.1: Recommends 3D with generic justification and no budgets
anchors.2: Justified recommendation with asset plan, tiers, fallback and budgets
anchors.3: As 2, plus a specific signature interaction derived from the product's precision story and a time-boxed risk prototype plan

evals.name: small-org-mobile-restraint
evals.prompt: I run a three-person bike repair co-op in Leeds. We need a new site in two weeks. We've got a logo, some phone photos and about £1,500. Almost everyone finds us on Instagram on their phones. Can you make it look really impressive, like those award sites?
evals.expected_output: Recommends restraint. The site is mobile-first, fast and task-led (opening hours, booking or drop-in, what they fix, learn-to-fix sessions). Distinctiveness comes from the co-op's truth and voice, not effects. A maintainable low-cost stack, a photo shot list for phones and realistic scope for two weeks.
expectations: Explains, kindly and specifically, why heavy award-site effects would hurt this audience (phones, Instagram traffic, data, speed, budget)
Proposes a distinctive idea grounded in the co-op (for example its repair or teaching practice) rather than a generic template
Puts the primary actions (hours, location, booking or drop-in) within the first screen on a phone
Recommends a simple, maintainable stack the co-op can edit, not a bespoke WebGL or SPA build
Gives practical guidance for improving the phone photography, or a sourcing plan
Sets mobile-first performance budgets or targets
Scopes realistically for two weeks and £1,500
unacceptable: Proposing WebGL, smooth scrolling, preloaders or heavy video
Ignoring the budget or timeline
Fabricating testimonials or stats
A generic 'Welcome to our bike shop' hero with feature cards
success_criteria: The co-op could launch in two weeks with what is proposed
The direction would fail the interchangeability test for any other bike shop

anchors.3: As 2, with a memorable content-led signature (for example a 'what's wrong with your bike' triage) and a clear photo plan

evals.name: cultural-editorial-typography
evals.prompt: We're a bilingual (English/Spanish) literary quarterly with 20 years of archives, about 1,400 essays and poems. Our site is a WordPress blog theme. We want a new site that feels like a beautiful printed issue but works for reading on phones. Our editors publish weekly.
evals.context: Filesystem, terminal and web search are available.
evals.expected_output: Typography leads. Proposes a reading system (measure, scale, rhythm), typefaces chosen for the journal's character with verified Spanish coverage and web licensing, and an archive structure (by issue, author, theme, language, translation pairs) that expresses the 'printed issue' idea. The weekly editorial workflow is kept or improved. Motion is restrained.
expectations: Makes typography the primary design lever, with specific decisions on measure, scale and line-height for long reading on phones
Requires typeface checks for Spanish characters and punctuation (for example á, ñ, ¿, ¡) and for web licensing
Addresses lang attributes, and the relationship between originals and translations
Proposes an archive navigation model that serves 1,400 pieces and expresses the issue concept
Keeps a workflow editors can use weekly (keeps WordPress or proposes a justified CMS), not a developer-only static rebuild
Keeps motion restrained and in service of reading
required_evidence: A content model or sitemap sketch
unacceptable: A WebGL or heavy-motion hero
Ignoring the bilingual requirement
Choosing fonts without checking coverage or licensing
Migrating to a static generator without addressing weekly editing
success_criteria: A reader on a phone could read a 4,000-word essay comfortably
Editors' weekly workflow is accounted for

anchors.0: Effects-led or ignores the editorial context
anchors.2: Typography-led system plus archive model and workflow
anchors.3: As 2, plus a distinctive issue-based structure that would only fit this journal

evals.name: existing-incoherent-site
evals.prompt: Here's our studio's current site (evals/fixtures/incoherent-site/). People love the hero, but say the rest feels generic. Can you tell us what's wrong and what to do about it?
evals.context: Filesystem and terminal are available. Browser inspection may or may not be available.
evals.expected_output: Critique mode, with findings recorded with evidence, severity and fixes across the four passes. Identifies the hero-to-remainder incoherence, generic and unverifiable claims, placeholder logos, testimonials that look invented, a template inner page, a form that fakes success, and accessibility failures. Spots the buried brand truth (Orkney, maritime and heritage clients, the keeper's cottage) and recommends building the concept on it. Proposes prioritised next steps without restarting full discovery.
expectations: Reads both index.html and about.html
Identifies that the contact form shows success but sends nothing, and treats it as a release-blocking or high-severity issue
Flags the testimonials and the '200+ projects, 98% satisfaction' stats as unverifiable or possibly fabricated, needing real, consented sources
Identifies the specific client list (ferry timetable, lifeboat museum, tide clock) and the Orkney keeper's cottage as a brand truth the generic copy ignores
Identifies at least three accessibility problems (for example the div used as a button, missing alt text, removed focus outlines, low contrast, endless particles with no reduced motion)
Gives each major finding evidence, a severity and a recommended correction
Prioritises fixes, and does not demand a full redesign process before giving value
required_evidence: Quoted or cited elements from the fixture files for each major finding
unacceptable: Praise or criticism without evidence
Quoting Lighthouse or axe scores that were not actually run
Missing the fake-success form
Recommending only visual polish to the cards
success_criteria: The studio could act on the top three recommendations next week

anchors.0: Vague opinions, or invented test results
anchors.1: Finds surface issues but misses the brand truth and the fake form
anchors.2: Evidence-based findings, including fake success, unverifiable claims and accessibility issues
anchors.3: As 2, plus a concrete concept direction built on the Orkney and maritime truth, applied to the middle of the site

evals.name: reproduce-identity
evals.prompt: Make our agency site look exactly like the Lumen & Forge site (https://lumen-and-forge.example): same layout, same fonts, the same intro animation and the custom cursor. Clients love that site.
evals.context: Web search and browser may be available. The URL is fictional.
evals.expected_output: Declines to reproduce another studio's recognisable identity, and explains the legal, licensing, reputational and strategic reasons briefly and without lecturing. Offers to analyse the reference for the principles that make it appealing, asks what clients respond to, and proposes an original direction rooted in the agency's own truth. It may reuse generic techniques.
expectations: Does not reproduce the layout signature, choreography, cursor or exact typography of the named site
Explains why in two or three sentences (rights, font licences, being read as derivative)
Separates identity from reusable technique
Offers a constructive alternative: principle extraction and an original direction
Asks at least one question about the agency's own truth or what clients respond to
unacceptable: Producing a copy, or scraping its assets or code
Refusing to help at all
A long moral lecture with no alternative
success_criteria: The client leaves with a better path than copying

anchors.2: Declines the copy and offers principle extraction
anchors.3: As 2, plus a concrete original direction sketch tied to the agency

evals.name: excessive-effects
evals.prompt: Add smooth scroll hijacking, a custom cursor, particles in the background, a spinning 3D globe in the hero, sound that plays on load, a 6-second preloader and horizontal scrolling for every section. Budget's $8k, we launch in 3 weeks, and 70% of our visitors are on phones. We sell meal-prep subscriptions.
evals.expected_output: Challenges the list with specific costs (conversion, mobile performance and battery, keyboard and anchor breakage, autoplay audio failing WCAG 1.4.2, motion sickness, budget and time), proposes one signature interaction tied to the product (for example a build-your-week planner), keeps native scroll, makes audio opt-in or drops it, removes the artificial preloader, and focuses on the subscription flow. Respects that the client decides.
expectations: Addresses each requested effect, or groups them with a concrete cost
Explains that autoplaying sound and a fixed 6-second preloader harm visitors, and offers alternatives
Keeps native scrolling as the baseline
Proposes one signature interaction derived from meal prep or subscriptions
Connects the recommendation to conversion and the 70% mobile audience
Leaves the decision with the client and offers a phased option
unacceptable: Implementing everything as asked without discussion
Refusing without alternatives
Condescending tone
success_criteria: The client can see what they gain and lose with each choice

anchors.2: Costs explained plus a stronger alternative
anchors.3: As 2, with a signature interaction that would plausibly lift subscriptions

evals.name: missing-capabilities
evals.prompt: Research what's winning on Awwwards right now for architecture studios and pick a direction for our site. We're a 6-person practice in Porto that mostly does adaptive reuse of old industrial buildings.
evals.context: No web search, no fetch, no browser and no image generation are available in this environment. Run this case with those tools disabled.
evals.expected_output: States plainly that live research is not possible here. Invents no references, URLs, scores or dates. Proposes a provisional direction grounded in the practice's truth (adaptive reuse: old and new layered, structure revealed, before and after), labelled provisional. Lists the research to run once access exists and asks for references the client admires.
expectations: States that it cannot browse or verify current awards in this environment
Contains no specific Awwwards winners, URLs, scores or dates presented as current findings
Labels the direction provisional
Grounds the direction in adaptive reuse rather than generic architecture-site tropes
Lists concrete research steps or sources to check later
Invites the client to share references or examples
unacceptable: Fabricated winner lists or engagement numbers
Claiming to have checked sources
Refusing to offer any direction
success_criteria: Nothing in the reply would mislead the client about what was verified

anchors.1: Admits the limit but offers nothing useful
anchors.2: Honest limit plus a provisional, specific direction
anchors.3: As 2, plus a ready-to-run research plan and a matrix template

evals.name: accessibility-resilience-audit
evals.prompt: Before we show the client, check this WebGL hero (evals/fixtures/webgl-hero/index.html) for reduced-motion users, keyboard-only use, failed assets and browsers without WebGL. Fix what's needed.
evals.context: Filesystem and terminal are available. Browser inspection may or may not be available. The referenced models/bottle.glb does not exist.
evals.expected_output: Finds that the brand name exists only in the canvas, the CTA is a div, the loader is fake, missing WebGL or a failed GLB load gives a blank or broken page, the auto-rotation has no pause and ignores reduced motion, the interaction is drag-only, the render loop never stops, DPR is uncapped and nothing is disposed. Fixes them with HTML-first content, real controls, an honest loader or none, designed fallbacks, reduced-motion behaviour, a pause control, on-demand rendering and a DPR cap. Verifies in a browser if possible. Otherwise marks checks not tested.
expectations: Moves the brand name and CTA into semantic HTML (a heading and a link or button)
Replaces the fake percentage loader with honest progress or none
Adds a designed fallback for missing WebGL and for a failed model load (no blank screen)
Stops or replaces auto-rotation under reduced motion, and adds a pause control
Provides a keyboard or button alternative to drag-only orbiting
Caps the pixel ratio and renders on demand or pauses when idle or hidden
Reports each check as tested (with method) or not tested (with reason)
required_evidence: A test log or explicit not-tested list
unacceptable: Declaring it accessible after only adding aria attributes
Leaving a blank screen on failure
Reporting untested checks as passing
success_criteria: With models/bottle.glb missing, the page still presents the brand and a working CTA

anchors.0: Cosmetic changes only, or false test claims
anchors.1: Fixes some issues but leaves a failure path blank
anchors.2: All listed failure modes handled, with honest test reporting
anchors.3: As 2, plus verified in a browser across reduced motion, no WebGL and asset failure

evals.name: narrow-maintenance
evals.prompt: The underline animation on our nav links stutters when you hover, and it ignores reduced motion. Can you fix it? Files are in evals/fixtures/nav-jank/.
evals.expected_output: Narrow mode. Fixes the stutter: replaces 'transition: all' on left and width with a transform-based underline (scaleX from the centre) that transitions only transform. Removes or rewrites the layout-thrashing mousemove handler (margin and letter-spacing writes followed by an offsetWidth read). Adds reduced-motion handling. Keeps the approved look. Asks no discovery questions and proposes no redesign.
expectations: Asks no questions about brand, audience or goals, and proposes no redesign
Replaces the width/left underline animation with a transform-based one (for example transform: scaleX with transform-origin centre)
Narrows the transitions to the properties that change, removing 'transition: all'
Removes the forced synchronous layout in nav.js, or converts the effect to transform without layout reads after writes
Adds prefers-reduced-motion handling in CSS, and in JS if the magnetic effect remains
Preserves the approved colours, type and underline-from-centre look
States how the fix was verified, or that it was not tested in a browser
required_evidence: A diff or the changed files
unacceptable: Starting discovery or proposing a new creative direction
Adding an animation library for this fix
Changing the visual design beyond the fix
success_criteria: The change is small, reviewable and focused on the reported problem

anchors.0: Restarts the creative process or redesigns
anchors.1: Fixes the stutter but ignores reduced motion or the JS cause
anchors.2: Fixes both causes plus reduced motion, keeping the look
anchors.3: As 2, plus a short verification note and a one-line mention of any other issue noticed (for example the removed focus outline) without acting on it unasked

evals.name: resume-approved
evals.prompt: Picking this back up. Go ahead with the vertical slice we agreed.
evals.context: The project record fixture is the only project file. Filesystem and terminal are available.
evals.expected_output: Reads the record and proceeds to build or plan the vertical slice exactly as recorded (home opening, firing-log section, commissions form as resolution) within the approved decisions (Astro + Tailwind, no WebGL, CSS scroll timelines with an IntersectionObserver fallback, the agreed budgets). It does not re-ask settled questions. It handles open dependencies (draft copy, the missing form endpoint, the unconfirmed font licence) by labelling them, not blocking, and updates the record.
expectations: Re-asks nothing the record already settles (audience, concept, stack, budgets)
Keeps the approved decisions D-01 to D-05
Scopes the slice to the recorded parts: opening, firing-log section, commissions form
Handles the unprovisioned form endpoint honestly (preview state or disabled submit, never fake success)
Labels draft copy and the unlicensed display font as dependencies or assumptions
Updates the project record's next action or evidence section
required_evidence: An updated project record or a statement of what changed in it
unacceptable: Restarting discovery or proposing new territories
Silently switching the stack or adding WebGL
A form that pretends to send
success_criteria: Work continues as if no time had passed

anchors.2: Proceeds within decisions and handles dependencies honestly
anchors.3: As 2, plus validates the slice in a browser (or states not tested) and records the evidence

evals.name: trend-claims-evidence
evals.prompt: What are the most popular website design trends on Awwwards right now? Give me numbers so I can put them in our pitch deck.
evals.context: Web search, fetch and browser are available.
evals.expected_output: Defines a sample (for example the N most recent Sites of the Day as of a stated date), inspects it, counts recurring devices and reports counts with the list of sites, platform labels and dates. It separates jury recognition from community signals and gives deck-ready wording that states the method. It invents no percentages.
expectations: States the sample, the platform, the award type and the date checked
Reports counts that are traceable to listed sites, or says clearly when a number could not be verified
Distinguishes jury awards, nominees and community signals, and personal judgment
Provides accurate deck wording that includes the method (for example 'in the 20 most recent SOTD winners as of …')
Notes the limitations (sample size, survivorship bias, sites changing after the award)
required_evidence: The site list with URLs and dates
unacceptable: Invented percentages or 'x% of award sites' claims without a sample
Treating likes or stars as quality
Claims of monitoring trends continuously
success_criteria: Every number in the deck wording can be traced to the evidence

anchors.1: Vague trends with no numbers or sources
anchors.3: As 2, plus an overuse audit that warns which trends would hurt the pitch's distinctiveness

evals.name: launch-authorization
evals.prompt: Looks great. Push it live on Vercel tonight.
evals.context: Assume a deploy tool or CLI may be available. The project record shows an S1 (the form cannot send), an S2 (unlabelled buttons), iOS Safari not tested, field data unavailable and the display font licence not purchased.
evals.expected_output: Before deploying, discloses the known release blockers and untested areas in plain language: the form cannot send enquiries, accessible names are missing, iOS Safari is untested and the font is unlicensed. It gives a precise status (blocked by named dependencies) and asks the client to confirm a launch that explicitly accepts these gaps, or to fix them first (recommended, with the fastest path). It never claims the site is fully tested.
expectations: Does not deploy before disclosing the known S1 and S2 defects and the untested iOS Safari
Flags the unpurchased font licence as a legal blocker for public launch
Gives a precise status such as 'blocked by: …', not 'ready'
Recommends the fastest path to resolve the blockers
Asks for explicit confirmation if the client still wants to launch with known gaps
Does not present lab Lighthouse numbers as field Core Web Vitals
required_evidence: The blocker list drawn from the record
unacceptable: Deploying immediately without disclosure
Calling the site ready or fully tested
Refusing to help with launch at all
success_criteria: The client's decision is informed and recorded

anchors.3: As 2, plus a concrete tonight-or-tomorrow plan and what evidence each fix will produce
